passage:
Monday. When the coach announced Indu as captain, Vaibhav clapped and smiled and felt as if he'd swallowed a stone. He had wanted it since Class 8. In the group chat he typed "She's good at speaking, not sure about tactics" and then deleted it.

The next Saturday. He watched Indu at practice: she arrived early, learned the juniors' names, changed the drill when someone struggled. It irritated him. It also, unwillingly, taught him something.

Three weeks later. He told his brother, "I'm jealous." It was easier to say aloud. That evening he stayed after practice to work on his passing, and asked Indu to time him.

qa.q: What did Vaibhav type in the group chat and then delete?
qa.a: "She's good at speaking, not sure about tactics".

qa.q: What was Vaibhav feeling when the coach announced Indu as captain?
qa.a: Envy and disappointment. He smiled and clapped but felt as if he'd swallowed a stone, since he had wanted the role since Class 8.

qa.q: What did Vaibhav do that helped him move forward?
qa.a: He admitted his jealousy to his brother, studied what Indu did well and kept practising, instead of sabotaging her or spreading doubts.

qa.q: How might Indu feel when Vaibhav asks her to time him?
qa.a: Probably surprised and pleased. It is a sign of respect, and it may show her that he has accepted the situation and wants to work together.

grounding: A rival gets the captaincy the protagonist wanted; he admits the envy, learns from her and keeps working.

passage:
When they announced Gopika's name as house captain, I clapped. My stomach, though, felt like I'd swallowed a stone. I'm Arohi, and I'd wanted that badge since Class 8.

For about a day I let myself be sour. I told my cousin it was unfair, that Gopika was just good at speeches. Then, in the corridor, I heard two juniors say, "Arohi should've got it, Gopika's only popular," and I realised how easy it would be to agree and let that spread. I didn't. I just walked off.

That evening I made myself be honest: I was jealous, plain and simple. So I wrote down what Gopika actually did. She organised the inter-house quiz from scratch. She learnt the names of every Class 6 kid. I hadn't done either.

This term I'm running the sports day sign-ups. It's not a badge. It's practice.

qa.q: What did Gopika learn the names of?
qa.a: Gopika learnt the names of every Class 6 kid.

qa.q: How can you tell Arohi felt jealous when Gopika's name was announced?
qa.a: Arohi clapped, but felt a stone-like weight in the stomach and later admitted to being plain jealous.

qa.q: What went right when Arohi overheard the juniors?
qa.a: Arohi chose not to agree or spread the doubts about Gopika, and walked off instead of feeding the rumour.

qa.q: How might Gopika see Arohi in the months after the election?
qa.a: If Gopika notices Arohi running the sports day sign-ups, she may see a capable, fair rival rather than a bitter one.

grounding: It shows a teen who feels envy in the stomach when a rival gets the captain spot, admits it, studies what the rival did well and keeps working.

passage:
Coach's note, district badminton squad, week 6

Vidya has taken over as first seed from Yogesh after beating him in the trials. He did not take it quietly. On Monday he skipped the cool-down and sat on the steps holding his stomach, saying he felt sick. I think it was the ranking more than lunch.

On Tuesday I heard him tell another player that Vidya's win was "a fluke on a slippery court." I asked to see him after practice. I did not scold him. I asked what Vidya did that he didn't. He was silent, then said, "She kept me moving to the back corners."

On Thursday he asked me for the trial video. He watched Vidya's footwork twice and has been drilling back-corner clears since. He even asked her for a rally session on Saturday. I will keep an eye on it, but this looks like a better direction.

qa.q: Who took over as first seed after the trials?
qa.a: Vidya took over as first seed from Yogesh.

qa.q: What does Yogesh holding his stomach on the steps suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he felt a sharp envy and hurt about losing first seed, felt in his body more than in words.

qa.q: How did the coach help Yogesh move away from spreading doubts?
qa.a: The coach asked what Vidya did that Yogesh didn't, which turned his attention from blaming the court to learning from her play.

qa.q: What is it like for Vidya when Yogesh asks her for a rally session?
qa.a: Vidya may feel respected and relieved that the tension is easing, especially if she had heard the fluke comment.

grounding: It shows a rival's win landing in the stomach, the pull towards spreading doubt, and a turn to studying what the rival did well.
